$comment: The patch registry: every Slang defect this repository has found, and what became of it. The single source of truth; the index of docs/upstream.md is generated from it (pwsh tools/ci/patch-registry.ps1 -Write) and checked against it in lint. Fields and states: AGENTS.md#patches.

defects.title: `spReflectionType_GetElementCount` / `GetSpecializedElementCount` crash on an array sized by a link-time constant
`getBindingRangeCount` throws a C++ exception through `extern "C"` for a resource array sized by a link-time constant
`spReflection_specializeGeneric` access-violates on a mismatched argument list
`spReflection_specializeType` on a non-generic type segfaults on Linux (an assert that removes its own check)
A constant buffer whose block holds only link-time-sized arrays gets no binding
A 64-bit 3/4-component vertex input is given one location; Vulkan requires two
`sample` interpolation without `SampleRateShading` (reported by others as #12441)
`float4x4` vertex input with a member `Offset` decoration
A missing `slang-glslang` is an error diagnostic on a successful result, reported once per global session
Windows: downstream libraries are not looked up in the compiler's own directory
Two public functions have C++ linkage
defects.state: not patchable: the fix gives both functions C linkage, which renames their exported symbols and breaks every C++ binary linked against them; keeping the old mangled export beside a C one needs a second declaration of the same name with another linkage, which C++ does not allow in one program without linker aliasing

defects.title: `ISession::loadModule*` returns a borrowed reference; the header does not say so
Releasing a session's last reference from `~Linkage` destroys the global session inside it
defects.state: known issue: macOS only and last measured on v2026.14.1; re-measuring needs a Mac; left to Slang (owner decision)

defects.title: `isBinaryModuleUpToDate` answers from the session's file cache
Reflection queries that answer nothing, and facts reflection does not carry
defects.state: known issue: small reflection gaps, several possibly by design, each answered by another route the binding reads; the one with a clear defect, the parameter block's space offset, is U33 and patched (owner decision: the moderate and large defects patched, the rest known issues)

defects.title: `linkWithOptions` silently ignores most compiler options
SPIR-V for `SV_VertexID` differs between x86-64 and aarch64 builds
GLSL: a hull shader's patch-constant function returns its struct with a bare `return;`
GLSL: a domain shader's per-vertex input is sized by the patch, which GLSL forbids
WGSL: a `const` is initialised from an `override`
WGSL: a matrix vertex input is written at one `@location`
defects.state: known issue: the fix splits a matrix vertex input into one location per column and reassembles it, a varying-legalization feature (the TODO at slang-ir-legalize-varying-params.cpp:880); left to Slang (owner decision)

defects.title: WGSL: arrays of textures and samplers are written as `binding_array` with no `enable`
defects.state: not patchable: binding_array is not in the WGSL specification; naga takes it behind enable wgpu_binding_array and Tint behind requires sized_binding_array, so no one text is valid for both, and choosing a WGSL dialect is a Slang design decision (Slang #13914 proposes one)

defects.title: An internal error where a diagnostic belongs: double on WGSL and Metal, varyings on CPU and CUDA
C++: the prelude has no vector arithmetic or comparison for `half`
WGSL: 64-bit integers are written as `u64`, which WGSL does not have
defects.state: not patchable: WGSL has no 64-bit integer; diagnosing u64 breaks the naga users Slang emits it for, and keeping it breaks Tint, so the fix is the WGSL dialect choice Slang #13914 proposes, which is the maintainers' design decision

defects.title: Metal: a texture read is called with an overload Metal does not declare
defects.state: known issue: a Metal texture read overload; measured only on the macos-15 runner, the fix needs Metal-side investigation; left to Slang (owner decision)

defects.title: Metal: an unbounded resource array is written as a flexible array member
defects.state: known issue: unbounded resource arrays need Metal argument buffers, a feature (Slang #11970); left to Slang (owner decision)

defects.title: Metal: a matrix vertex input at one `[[attribute]]`
defects.state: known issue: the same matrix-varying feature as U21, for Metal; left to Slang (owner decision)

defects.title: Metal: an array of device pointers as a kernel input
defects.state: known issue: device-pointer arrays as kernel inputs need an argument-buffer lowering, a feature; left to Slang (owner decision)

defects.title: A component type linked a second time ignores the second link's options
A second module loaded from source at an already-used path ends in an internal assert
C++: an append or consume structured buffer ends in an internal error
A top-level parameter block's sub-object range reports space offset 0
GLSL: the tessellation stages declare no `layout(vertices = N) out` or input primitive
GLSL: a hull shader's per-vertex output is indexed with `uint(gl_InvocationID)`
A standard module records its source as a path relative to Slang's build tree, resolved from wherever the module is loaded
defects.state: known issue: the stray file is only named among the dependency files, never read: a broken one there leaves the compile unchanged; the fix is in how Slang compiles the standard modules (owner decision: the moderate and large defects patched, the rest known issues)
